summary: This lecture continues the torture of the companions, this time the wealthy and high-ranking. The ustaz mentions Uthman ibn Affan, rolled in a mat and burned by his family, and Suhaib ar-Rumi, beaten until unconscious. The main story is Mus'ab ibn Umair, a very rich young Meccan known for costly clothes and perfume. Seeing the steadfastness of Bilal and Zinnirah, he went to Dar al-Arqam and embraced Islam, but Uthman ibn Talhah told his mother. Mus'ab's mother chained him up with little food, yet he refused to leave Islam. The ustaz explains why Mus'ab was not whipped publicly, and closes with the Prophet SAW again telling Abu Talib he would not stop even if the sun were placed in his right hand.
keyPoints: The wealthy and high-ranking were also tortured, like Uthman ibn Affan, rolled in a mat and burned.
Mus'ab ibn Umair, a rich and famous youth, embraced Islam at Dar al-Arqam after seeing Bilal's and Zinnirah's steadfastness.
Mus'ab's mother locked him up and reduced his food and clothing, but he did not leave Islam.
Mus'ab was not whipped in public because his mother loved him and his many followers would have questioned it.
The Prophet SAW told Abu Talib he would not stop until Allah gave him victory or he died.

chapters.title: Opening and the Prophet's answer
chapters.summary: The ustaz begins with the Prophet's words to Abu Talib and continues the story of tortured companions.

chapters.title: The family of Yasir and the high-ranking
chapters.summary: Sumayyah was the first martyr, and not only slaves but high-ranking people were tortured too.

chapters.title: Uthman ibn Affan rolled and burned
chapters.summary: Uthman, the third caliph, was rolled in a mat and burned beneath it to make him abandon the Prophet SAW, but he endured.

chapters.title: Suhaib ar-Rumi
chapters.summary: Suhaib was beaten until unconscious and did not know what he said.

chapters.title: The wealthy Mus'ab ibn Umair
chapters.summary: Mus'ab came from a millionaire family, wore clothes ordered from Yemen and special shoes, and was followed by many youths.

chapters.title: Seeing the companions' steadfastness
chapters.summary: Mus'ab saw Bilal and Zinnirah endure and asked why they did not surrender, then sought information about Islam.

chapters.title: Dar al-Arqam
chapters.summary: Mus'ab knocked on the door of the secret house, was invited in by the Prophet SAW and embraced Islam after hearing his teaching.

chapters.title: Told to keep Islam secret
chapters.summary: Rich converts faced business losses, and Khabbab who was burned had been tortured by his mistress Umm Anmar, who later suffered illness.

chapters.title: Keep quiet and pray secretly
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW told Mus'ab to keep it secret and he prayed quietly with the companions, fewer than forty.

chapters.title: Uthman ibn Talhah tells
chapters.summary: Uthman ibn Talhah saw Mus'ab pray and told his mother.

chapters.title: Mus'ab's mother
chapters.summary: His mother did not believe at first, but Mus'ab admitted it and invited her to Islam.

chapters.title: Locked up and starved
chapters.summary: His mother had the guards chain him in a small room, giving little food and taking his clothes and gold.

chapters.title: No turning back
chapters.summary: Mus'ab told them to take all his wealth but refused to leave the Prophet SAW, and would escape to Abyssinia.

chapters.title: Why he was not whipped publicly
chapters.summary: His mother loved him and Mus'ab had many followers who would question it, unlike slaves who had no defenders.

chapters.title: Abu Talib and the sun in the right hand
chapters.summary: Quraysh asked Abu Talib to stop him, but he said he would not stop and Abu Talib promised to stay with him.

chapters.title: Recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz recaps the stories of Uthman, Suhaib and Mus'ab, and promises the story of the flight to Abyssinia.

sirah.summary: This lecture covers the torture of Uthman, Suhaib and Mus'ab ibn Umair and the Prophet's reply to Abu Talib.

lessons.title: The high-ranking are tested too
lessons.body: Not only slaves were tortured but also the rich and high-ranking.

lessons.title: Steadfastness draws hearts
lessons.body: Mus'ab was drawn to Islam by the steadfastness of the tortured companions.

lessons.title: A clean heart accepts the truth
lessons.body: Mus'ab embraced Islam because his heart was clean and good.

lessons.title: The wisdom of keeping quiet for a while
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW told Mus'ab to keep his Islam secret because of various threats.

lessons.title: Leaving luxury for faith
lessons.body: Mus'ab told them to take all his wealth but would not leave the Prophet SAW.

lessons.title: Allah repays the oppressor
lessons.body: Umm Anmar who burned Khabbab was struck by an illness treated with fire.

lessons.title: Not stopping the call
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW would not stop until Allah gave him victory or he died.

lessons.title: Sincere family support
lessons.body: Abu Talib promised to stay with him though he did not embrace Islam.
